weights.csoNote: Kept UNCONDITIONAL (despite the prompt's pinWhen suggestion) to honour DEFG — ALWAYS check capillary glucose in ANY confusion; the glucose VALUE in vitals is the definitive trigger. Uganda: hypoglycaemia is frequently NON-diabetic — severe malaria, sepsis, alcohol, liver failure, prolonged sulfonylurea — so a diabetes-only pin would under-surface it.
weights.weightCitation: ADA Standards of Care 2024; WHO Guidelines for Malaria 2025 (hypoglycaemia in severe malaria); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Uganda: infection is a leading cause of delirium — systemic sepsis, bacterial/cryptococcal/TB meningitis, HSV encephalitis. LP + cultures; do not delay empirical antibiotics +/- aciclovir; meningococcal rash is non-blanching.
weights.weightCitation: Surviving Sepsis Campaign; Sepsis-3 (Singer M et al., JAMA 2016); WHO meningitis guidance; Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Focal signs + sudden onset; reduced consciousness + headache + vomiting suggests raised ICP/haemorrhage. CT distinguishes ischaemic vs haemorrhagic but is often unavailable in Uganda; reverse anticoagulation if bleeding.
weights.weightCitation: AHA/ASA stroke & intracerebral haemorrhage guidelines (2019/2022); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on FEVER (cerebral malaria without fever is essentially never). Holoendemic Uganda — any FEBRILE confusion needs a malaria RDT/smear and IV artesunate if severe. Check GLUCOSE (hypoglycaemia mimics/coexists — DEFG) and exclude concurrent meningitis (co-infection common).
weights.weightCitation: WHO Guidelines for Malaria (2025); Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL (diabetes / polyuria). The glucose VALUE in vitals is the definitive trigger; new-onset DKA may lack a diabetes flag, so polyuria/polydipsia also fires the pin. HHS (profound confusion + very high glucose + marked dehydration, often without ketosis) is the more confusion-predominant form. Check glucose + ketones.
weights.weightCitation: ADA/EASD/JBDS/AACE/DTS Consensus on Hyperglycaemic Crises (DKA/HHS), Diabetes Care 2024; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Alcohol withdrawal (tremor, autonomic features, withdrawal seizures, delirium tremens at 48-72h); opioid/sedative intoxication (naloxone if opioid). ALWAYS co-administer PARENTERAL THIAMINE (see Wernicke's) and check glucose.

Dementia is the CHRONIC, gradual, stable picture — an ACUTE or FLUCTUATING change is DELIRIUM until proven otherwise (delirium superimposed on dementia is common, so the acute change still needs a full reversible-cause workup, never attributed to 'known dementia'). Under-recognised in Uganda; consider HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder in younger patients.

CONDITIONAL on liver disease / hepatitis. Uganda: chronic liver disease from HEPATITIS B (endemic) and alcohol is common. Always seek + treat a PRECIPITANT (GI bleed, infection/SBP, constipation, diuretics, hypokalaemia). Asterixis is the key sign but is NOT a token; treat with lactulose; ammonia is supportive not diagnostic.
weights.weightCitation: AASLD-EASL Hepatic Encephalopathy guidelines; West Haven criteria; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on CKD — BUT acute kidney injury (severe malaria, sepsis, dehydration — all common in Uganda) causes uraemic encephalopathy WITHOUT a CKD flag, so the urea/creatinine LAB value is the real trigger and AKI risks being missed by a CKD-only pin. Asterixis/myoclonus/seizures; dialysis access is limited — treat reversible AKI causes urgently.
weights.weightCitation: KDIGO AKI Guideline; Davidson's 24th ed (uraemic encephalopathy)

weights.csoNote: The electrolyte VALUES (Na, Ca) are LAB-measured and NOT in the token set — recommend checking U&E in any confusion (like glucose). Severe/acute HYPONATRAEMIA causes cerebral oedema and seizures and must be corrected at a CONTROLLED rate (over-rapid correction -> osmotic demyelination). Also consider HYPERCALCAEMIA (malignancy, TB).

The SpO2 VALUE in vitals is the trigger — check oxygenation in any confusion. CO2 NARCOSIS (hypercapnic respiratory failure) causes drowsiness/confusion and can be WORSENED by uncontrolled high-flow oxygen (target 88-92% where there is hypercapnic risk). Few applicable risk tokens in this complaint — relies on the vitals SpO2 and the dyspnoea feature.
weights.weightCitation: BTS Guideline for oxygen use in adults; Davidson's 24th ed (hypoxia / hypercapnic CO2 narcosis)

weights.dx: HIV CNS disease (cryptococcal / toxoplasmosis / HIV encephalopathy)
weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on HIV/immunosuppression — basePrior population-dependent. Groups CRYPTOCOCCAL meningitis (commonest — CrAg, raised ICP needs serial therapeutic LPs), CNS TOXOPLASMOSIS (focal, ring-enhancing), HIV ENCEPHALOPATHY/HAND, plus TB meningitis/PML/CMV. In advanced HIV (CD4<100-200) a major cause of confusion in Uganda; LP + CrAg + CT + CD4.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Guidelines on cryptococcal disease in HIV & HIV/opportunistic infections; Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on alcohol — but ALSO occurs with malnutrition, prolonged vomiting/hyperemesis and refeeding (not all tokenised). CRITICAL: give PARENTERAL THIAMINE before/with glucose in any malnourished/alcoholic confused patient — glucose without thiamine can PRECIPITATE Wernicke's. The classic triad (confusion + ophthalmoplegia + ataxia) is usually INCOMPLETE; treatable but irreversible (Korsakoff) if missed. Ataxia is not a token; ophthalmoplegia ~ 'visual disturbance'.
weights.weightCitation: EFNS Guidelines on Wernicke encephalopathy; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on thyroid disease — uncommon, TWO opposite extremes. MYXOEDEMA COMA (severe HYPOthyroidism — hypothermia, bradycardia, reduced consciousness, often precipitated by infection/cold). THYROID STORM (severe HYPERthyroidism — fever, tachycardia, AF, agitation; Burch-Wartofsky). Both must-not-miss; the TEMPERATURE in vitals (low vs high) is a key discriminator; confirm with TFTs.
weights.weightCitation: American Thyroid Association guidance (Burch-Wartofsky for thyroid storm); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Head-trauma history (often TRIVIAL or forgotten) is NOT a capture token — recommend adding one. Classic FLUCTUATING consciousness +/- focal signs in the elderly/alcoholic/anticoagulated, often weeks after a minor head injury. CT is diagnostic (often unavailable in Uganda); surgically evacuable — a reversible cause not to miss.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's 24th ed; neurosurgical references (chronic subdural haematoma)
